# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 14 (Bu-Vb Pc14)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc14
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 14
**Title (English, from literature):** Leaving furniture outside
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 14 (*Mañcasanthārana*) is a disciplinary rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka concerning the care of communal property. The rule stipulates that a monk who spreads out or has someone spread out furniture belonging to the Saṅgha in an open space, and departs without packing it away or having it put away, incurs an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*). In the analysis of the rule's vocabulary, the text provides canonical definitions for various types of couches, including *masaraka*, *bundikābaddha*, *kulīrapādaka*, and *āhaccapādaka*, definitions that also serve to clarify parallel terminology in the *Khandhaka* literature [Horner]. Modern English translation of the rule is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
